gate: You hold the lantern steady while the choir of the sunk sings your name back to you.
A drowned face rises under the ice and you do not look away until it sinks.
The dark asks for the lantern and you refuse it, though the wick is nearly gone.
You bargain with the bell keeper for passage and give him a name you no longer use.
Something breathes behind the ossuary door and you keep your feet on the wet stone.
You witness the drowned watchman rise from his chair and you do not step back.
A voice in the cistern offers you the way out for your shadow and you refuse.
You defy the chain that hums at your throat and walk on through the humming hall.
The rust whispers that the others have left you and you resist the urge to run.
You bargain with the thing under the ferry for a crossing and it asks for your voice.
You witness the choir of the sunk open their eyes and you keep counting the steps.
The lantern gutters to a blue bead and you sit in the black until it climbs again.
A hand of green bone closes on your ankle and you refuse to cry out in the flooded hall.
The drowned bell says lie down and you climb the salt stair instead.
The salt on the wall spells your mother's name and you walk past it without a word.
You resist the sleep the cold offers as the water reaches your chest.
You bargain with the keeper of the chains for a key and give up the hour of your birth.
You witness the sunk ship turn over in the black and you do not lose count of the rope.
A door of ribs asks for your true name before it opens and you give it silence.
You stand in the drowned chapel while the water sings and you do not add your voice.
You keep your hand on the drowned sailor's chest while their heart starts again.
The dark holds its breath around you and you hold yours longer.
A cold hand takes yours in the flooded hall and you walk on without letting go.
A whisper offers you the name of the next to die and you refuse to hear it.
Your own voice calls from the bottom of the well and you do not answer it.
The lantern shows a shape standing behind you in the water and you do not turn.
The walls close a finger's width with every breath and you breathe slow.
You sleep a full hour on the salt ledge while the dark moves around you.
Children's laughter comes from the flooded nursery and you keep walking past the door.
The rope creaks as it takes your weight over the pit and you trust it anyway.
Eyes open in the ossuary wall as you pass and you keep your pace even.
A hand on your shoulder pulls you toward the water and you stand until it lets go.
You let the eel wind round your wrist until it loses interest and swims off.
A drowned knight lowers a sword across the path and you step over it.
The silence after the bell is so long you begin to count, and you keep counting.
The water whispers the day you will die and you ask it for the hour too.
You stand your ground as the flood comes down the stair toward you and stops.
The floor drops away under your lantern and you walk the plank of light it leaves.
Your reflection in the black pool steps away first and you do not follow it.
The thing in the well climbs a rung for each lie you tell, and you tell none.
chain: You hold your breath as the choir passes, then hold your nerve when it stops beside you.
You refuse the cistern voice once, and when it wears a friend's face you refuse again.
You bargain with the ferryman for passage, then keep your word when the far bank moves.
You witness the drowned rise from their pews, then walk the aisle between them.
You resist the cold's soft bargain at the knees, then resist it again at the throat.
You defy the bell that says kneel, then defy the chain that reaches out to make you.
You sit with the dying lantern through the black, and when it wakes you are still there.
You give the door of ribs your name, then stand while it says it back in a drowned voice.
You wait out the first scream in the dark, then walk toward the second.
You let the drowned hand hold your wrist, then lead it back to the water.
You find the old bones in the cell, then sit beside them until your hands stop shaking.
You drink from the cup the drowned priest offers, then refuse the second.
You wake alone in the black hall, then light the lantern with steady hands.
You climb toward the sound of weeping, then find the courage to climb past it.
You look into the drowned face under the glass, then look long enough to learn it.
You hold the door while the dark pushes, then hold it after the pushing stops.
You cross the plank above the pit, then turn and cross back for the one who froze.
You hear the tide coming through the tunnels, then choose to wait for it here.
You keep the lantern lit through the gale in the shaft, then give its light away.
You bear the cold of the flooded crypt, then bear the silence in the room past it.
You let the rats run over your boots, then over your hands on the ladder.
You face the thing at the end of the tunnel, then walk up to it and find a coat.
You sing to keep the choir away, then keep singing when your voice starts to shake.
You go down into the flooded vault, then down again when the first stair ends.
You keep watch over the dying keeper all night, then carry their lantern out at dawn.
You hear the chain dragging behind you, then turn and hold your light up to it.
You wade toward the thing that splashes, then keep wading when it goes under.
You read the name on the fresh grave, then walk on though the name is yours.
You watch the others' lanterns go out one by one, then keep yours lit for them.
You step into the black water up to your knees, then to your waist, and go on.
You answer the riddle the dark asks, then refuse the prize it offers for it.
You bury the stranger you find in the silt, then say the words no one said for them.
You keep your eyes open as the ceiling groans, then step out as the dust falls.
You hold still while the blind thing sniffs your hand, then let it pass.
You ignore the knocking inside the coffin, then open it when the knocking stops.
You enter the room where the bell rang itself, then stay until it rings again.
You follow the sound of your own footsteps ahead, then catch up with them.
You let the dark close behind you, then go on without looking back once.
You keep your promise to the drowned child, then leave the doll where they asked.
You stop at the edge of the pit when the voice says jump, then step back from it.
